svg.title: Syn agreement during failure and disconnection
svg.desc: In a conventional equal-weight four-validator BFT committee, a connected quorum of three can progress subject to protocol conditions while one validator is unavailable. A two and two partition cannot finalise. Authors on disconnected devices can still save signed records and exchange them later, without claiming final community authority.
svg.text: Quorum finality and offline authorship have different limits
Illustrative conventional BFT committee: four equal validators, quorum three, at most one Byzantine fault
Three connected, one unavailable
A
B
C
D
The connected quorum can progress under engine assumptions.
The returning node verifies history before participating again.
Two connected on each side
A
B
C
D
Neither side can finalise with only two votes.
A permanent partition does not gain a deadline from aBFT.
People can still keep signed knowledge records
Alice records an observation offline. Bob records a conflicting account. Both retain authorship and evidence.
After reconnection, replicas exchange both records. A community-endorsed view applies its own explicit admission policy.
Local durability, signature verification, peer receipt and finalised endorsement are separate facts.
Quorum examples do not describe the thresholds of PoW, Snow protocols or arbitrary federated quorum systems.
Four processes sharing one administrator test the software; they do not establish four independent trust owners.
Original explanatory illustration · 23 October 2026 · no running network or benchmark is implied.
